metadata.topic: 3-tier Clean Architecture + MVVM for macOS transcription app

clean_architecture_swift.name: Interactor Pattern
clean_architecture_swift.description: Stateless business logic encapsulation that receives requests but never returns data directly. Forwards results to AppState or Binding.
clean_architecture_swift.source: Alexey Naumov - Clean Architecture for SwiftUI
clean_architecture_swift.applicability: High - fits OpenOats use case for transcription orchestration
clean_architecture_swift.code_example:
protocol CountriesInteractor { func loadCountries() }
struct RealCountriesInteractor: CountriesInteractor { let webRepository: CountriesWebRepository; let appState: AppState }

clean_architecture_swift.name: Repository Pattern
clean_architecture_swift.description: Abstract gateway for reading/writing data. Provides async API for CRUD operations. Stateless, no business logic, no AppState mutation.
clean_architecture_swift.applicability: High - perfect for multiple transcription backends (MLX, WhisperKit, AssemblyAI)
clean_architecture_swift.code_example:
protocol TranscriptionRepository { func transcribe(audioData: Data) -> AnyPublisher<String, Error> }
struct WhisperKitRepository: TranscriptionRepository { let session: URLSession }

clean_architecture_swift.name: AppState (Redux-like)
clean_architecture_swift.description: ObservableObject serving as single source of truth. Contains userData, routing, system state. Protocol-facaded for testability.
clean_architecture_swift.applicability: Medium - transcription state management needs careful design
clean_architecture_swift.code_example: class AppState: ObservableObject { @Published var userData = UserData(); @Published var routing = ViewRouting(); @Published var system = System() }

protocol_based_di.name: Protocol-Oriented Dependency Injection
protocol_based_di.description: Define protocols for each layer boundary. Inner layers declare protocols, outer layers implement. Uses DIP (Dependency Inversion Principle).
protocol_based_di.pattern: Inner circle declares protocol (TranscriptionService), outer circle implements (MLXTranscriptionService, WhisperKitService, AssemblyAIService)

protocol_based_di.name: Constructor Injection
protocol_based_di.description: Dependencies injected via init parameters. Enables testability and loose coupling.
protocol_based_di.applicability: High - all interactors and repositories should use constructor injection
protocol_based_di.code_example: struct RealCountriesInteractor: CountriesInteractor { let webRepository: CountriesWebRepository; let appState: AppState; init(webRepository: CountriesWebRepository, appState: AppState) { ... } }

protocol_based_di.name: Environment Injection (SwiftUI)
protocol_based_di.applicability: High - native SwiftUI approach for view layer
protocol_based_di.code_example: struct CountriesList: View { @EnvironmentObject var appState: AppState; @Environment(\.interactors) var interactors: InteractorsContainer }

swift_6_2_concurrency.name: Sendable Protocol
swift_6_2_concurrency.description: Marks types as safe to share across concurrency domains. Value types automatically Sendable. Reference types need explicit conformance.
swift_6_2_concurrency.applicability: Critical - all entities crossing boundaries must be Sendable
swift_6_2_concurrency.recommendation: Make all Domain layer entities (Transcription, AudioSegment) Sendable. Use @Sendable for closures passed across isolation boundaries.

swift_6_2_concurrency.name: Actor Isolation
swift_6_2_concurrency.description: Actors protect mutable state. MainActor for UI, custom actors for concurrent workloads.
swift_6_2_concurrency.applicability: High - transcription backends run on background, results on MainActor
swift_6_2_concurrency.pattern: @globalActor struct TranscriptionActor { static let shared = TranscriptionActor() }

swift_6_2_concurrency.name: MainActor
swift_6_2_concurrency.description: Ensures UI updates happen on main thread. @MainActor annotation on ViewModels and UI-related methods.
swift_6_2_concurrency.applicability: High - all SwiftUI view models should be @MainActor
swift_6_2_concurrency.code_example: @MainActor class TranscriptionViewModel: ObservableObject { @Published var transcription: String = "" }

swift_6_2_concurrency.name: Global Actors for Resources
swift_6_2_concurrency.description: Create custom global actors for shared resources like audio engines.
swift_6_2_concurrency.applicability: Medium - audio processing needs careful isolation
swift_6_2_concurrency.recommendation: Use @AudioActor for audio session management to prevent concurrent access issues.

clean_architecture_swiftui.name: Clean Architecture for SwiftUI (nalexn)
clean_architecture_swiftui.relevance: Primary reference - demonstrates the exact 3-tier pattern OpenOats needs
key_takeaways: Interactors should be stateless and protocol-facaded
Repositories provide async CRUD, no business logic
AppState as single source of truth with @Published properties
Full test coverage achievable with protocol-based DI

whisperkit.name: WhisperKit (argmaxinc)
features: On-device speech AI for Apple Silicon
whisperkit.relevance: Infrastructure layer reference - shows how to abstract multiple transcription backends
key_takeaways: Protocol-based abstraction for different model backends
Async/await API design for transcription operations

swift_combining.name: Clean Architecture + Combine Pattern
swift_combining.description: Using Combine Publishers for async operations between layers
swift_combining.pattern: Repositories return AnyPublisher<T, Error>, Interactors subscribe and update AppState
swift_combining.relevance: Alternative to async/await for streaming transcription results

clean_architecture_pitfalls.symptom: Simple features require changes in 10+ files
clean_architecture_pitfalls.mitigation: Start with 3 layers (Domain, Business, Infrastructure). Only split when complexity demands. Use feature-based organization within layers.

clean_architecture_pitfalls.symptom: Entities are just data bags with no behavior
clean_architecture_pitfalls.mitigation: Rich domain models with validation logic. Entities should encapsulate business invariants.
Strict dependency rule enforcement. Domain layer should be pure Swift with no external imports except maybe Foundation for basic types.

clean_architecture_pitfalls.symptom: Interactors grow to 500+ lines handling too many responsibilities
clean_architecture_pitfalls.mitigation: Split interactors by feature/use case. Follow SRP - one interactor per significant operation.
Generic repository base class with specialized implementations. Shared query builders for common operations.

swift_concurrency_pitfalls.symptom: Swift 6.2 StrictConcurrency warnings or runtime crashes
swift_concurrency_pitfalls.mitigation: Audit all types crossing concurrency boundaries. Make entities Sendable. Use actors for shared mutable state.
Heavy work on background actors, only UI updates on MainActor. Never call blocking APIs from @MainActor.

swift_concurrency_pitfalls.symptom: Inconsistent state when multiple calls interleave
swift_concurrency_pitfalls.mitigation: Design actors with reentrancy in mind. Use async let for parallel work. Check state after suspension points.

swift_concurrency_pitfalls.symptom: Missing or double resume of continuations
swift_concurrency_pitfalls.mitigation: Always use defer or finally blocks to ensure continuation is resumed exactly once. Consider using wrappers.

migration_pitfalls.symptom: Months of work with no shippable increments, regression risk
migration_pitfalls.mitigation: Strangler Fig pattern - incrementally extract features behind facade. Maintain working app throughout.

migration_pitfalls.symptom: Everything depends on everything, can't extract modules
migration_pitfalls.mitigation: Start with infrastructure (repositories) - easiest to extract with protocol boundaries. Then extract domain entities. Business logic (interactors) last.

migration_pitfalls.symptom: Existing tests break as you refactor
migration_pitfalls.mitigation: Maintain integration tests throughout. Add unit tests for extracted components. Use characterization tests to verify behavior preservation.

migration_pitfalls.symptom: Abstractions added before understanding domain, wrong boundaries
migration_pitfalls.mitigation: Extract working code first, then abstract. Let the domain guide the architecture, not the reverse.

strangler_fig.name: Strangler Fig Pattern
strangler_fig.description: Incrementally replace monolith by routing calls through facade to new architecture
steps: 1. Identify bounded contexts (transcription, audio processing, UI)
2. Create facade layer that routes to old or new implementation
3. Extract one context at a time starting with lowest coupling
4. Maintain working app at each step
5. Remove old code when context fully migrated

layer_first.name: Layer-by-Layer Extraction
layer_first.description: Extract horizontal layers starting from bottom (Infrastructure) up
layer_first.applicability: Good for OpenOats - clear infrastructure boundaries (MLX, WhisperKit, AssemblyAI)
recommended_order: 1. Infrastructure (Repositories) - Extract transcription backends first. Create protocol boundaries.
2. Domain (Entities) - Extract value objects and core business rules.
3. Business (Interactors) - Extract use cases. Most complex, depends on other layers.
4. Presentation (MVVM) - Refactor view models last after business layer stable.

feature_first.name: Feature-by-Feature Extraction
feature_first.description: Extract vertical slices (full stack features) one at a time
feature_first.example: Extract 'File Transcription' feature end-to-end, then 'Real-time Transcription'

rules: No imports of UIKit, SwiftUI, or external frameworks
All types must be Sendable for Swift 6.2 compatibility
Rich models with validation, not anemic data bags
Stateless - all state in injected AppState or returned via Binding
Async/await or Combine for async operations

contents: External Adapters: API clients for cloud services
rules: Handle all external dependencies (WhisperKit, MLX, URLSession)
Convert external errors to domain errors

contents: Views: SwiftUI views for transcription UI
ViewModels: @MainActor ObservableObjects that bridge to interactors
rules: Views are functions of state only - no business logic

multi_backend_strategy.protocol_design: protocol TranscriptionRepository: Sendable { func transcribe(audio: AudioData) async throws -> Transcription }
implementations: MLXTranscriptionRepository: Uses MLX Swift for local inference
AssemblyAIRepository: HTTP client for cloud API
multi_backend_strategy.selection_strategy: Interactor selects repository based on: availability (MLX/WhisperKit model loaded?), user preference, fallback chain (local first, cloud fallback)

sendable_requirements: All domain entities (Transcription, AudioSegment) conform to Sendable
All repository protocols require Sendable implementations
concurrency_strategy.pattern: async/await for transcription flow: ViewModel (MainActor) -> Interactor -> Repository (background actor) -> result back to MainActor

tasks: Create WhisperKitRepository wrapper (if not using directly)
Write unit tests for repositories with mocked dependencies
phase_1_infrastructure.success_criteria: Repositories extracted with passing tests, old code still works

phase_2_domain.success_criteria: Domain layer defined, no dependencies on outer layers

tasks: Migrate transcription orchestration logic from view models
Add progress reporting via Binding or AppState
phase_3_business.success_criteria: Business logic moved out of views, interactor tested

tasks: Move state to AppState where appropriate
phase_4_presentation.success_criteria: Clean MVVM with thin view models, full architecture in place
